analysis.evidence: Terah takes Abram, Lot, and Sarai, each introduced by the direct-object marker אֶת. The following clause says they set out from Ur for Canaan, showing that Terah took his relatives with him on the journey.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks the Qal wayyiqtol. The verb is third person masculine singular, agreeing with its subject תֶּרַח.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּקַּח תֶּרַח אֶת אַבְרָם בְּנוֹ reads “Terah took Abram his son.” The object marker אֶת introduces Abram, and בְּנוֹ identifies him as Terah’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of וַיִּקַּח, “he took.”
analysis.sense: The father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.definition: Abram, the earlier name of Abraham, son of Terah.

analysis.evidence: Terah is the subject of וַיִּקַּח, “took.” In אֶת אַבְרָם בְּנוֹ, “Abram his son,” בְּנוֹ identifies Abram as Terah’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת marks it as a direct object of וַיִּקַּח.
analysis.sense: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham

article.name: הָרָן
article.summary: Genesis 11:27 names Haran alongside Abram and Nahor as a son of Terah. It then identifies him as the father of Lot.

draft.definition: Haran, the personal name borne here by Terah’s son and Lot’s father.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 identifies Haran through both family relationships. The verse gives no derivation for his name.

analysis.evidence: לוֹט בֶּן הָרָן identifies Lot as Haran’s son. The following בֶּן בְּנוֹ, “his son’s son,” identifies Lot as Terah’s grandson through Haran. The verse gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The initial ה belongs to the name. The word has no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Haran, son of Terah and father of Lot

evidence.note: The verse explicitly gives Sarai as the name of Abram’s wife.
God identifies שָׂרַי as Abraham’s wife and gives her the name שָׂרָה.
Kings and their noblewomen appear in parallel. The noun for the women, שָׂרוֹת, is the plural of שָׂרָה.

article.name: שָׂרַי
article.summary: Sarai is the name by which Abram’s wife is introduced. Her later name שָׂרָה has the same form as the Hebrew noun for a princess or noblewoman, supporting a similar meaning for Sarai. The text leaves the force of the earlier name’s ending unexplained.

draft.definition: Sarai, the earlier name of Abram’s wife Sarah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:29 names Abram’s wife Sarai. Genesis 17:15 gives both names when God tells Abraham to call her Sarah.

analysis.evidence: וְאֵת marks שָׂרַי as another person Terah took with him. The following phrases כַּלָּתוֹ and אֵשֶׁת אַבְרָם identify Sarai as Terah’s daughter-in-law and Abram’s wife.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The final י is part of the name.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abram’s wife before she was named Sarah.
